issues.description: Check name 'single_network_interface' contradicts metadata's CheckID and PR title; algorithm reports on multi-NIC, not single-NIC.
issues.detail: The class, directory, and CheckID say 'single_network_interface' but the PR title and risk narrative describe detecting multiple interfaces. A careful reader cannot tell from the name what PASS means without running the code. Rename one or the other so the invariant 'PASS iff len(network_interfaces) == 1' is stated by the name itself.

issues.description: GKE-detection-by-name-prefix is a fragile heuristic; the invariant 'gke- prefix implies GKE-managed' is not stable.
issues.detail: Users can name any VM 'gke-anything' and silently obtain MANUAL status instead of FAIL, defeating the check. GCE exposes GKE membership via labels (goog-gke-node) or instance metadata; that is the correct data source. The current heuristic is asymptotically O(1) but semantically wrong, and the docstring promises behavior the data does not support.

issues.description: Loop invariant and zero-interface branch are not stated; the empty case silently returns PASS.
issues.detail: The check has three branches (=1, >1, else) but no comment stating the invariant maintained per iteration, and the 'no network interfaces' branch leaves status as PASS while reporting 'has no network interfaces.' That is a literate-programming gap: a reader cannot tell whether zero NICs is intentionally PASS or an oversight. State the invariant in one line and decide the zero case deliberately.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model discards accessConfigs/natIP, forcing future checks to re-parse the raw API response.
issues.detail: The data structure chosen (name, network, subnetwork) is the minimum for this check but throws away access configs already iterated in _get_instances. A subsequent check needing public-IP-per-NIC will either re-walk the API or duplicate the parsing. Pike's rule applies: pick the data structure that serves the next check too, not just this one.

issues.description: Mutable default argument 'network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []' on the Pydantic model.
issues.detail: Pydantic v1 handles this safely, but the literal '[]' default on a class attribute is the same shape as the classic Python mutable-default bug and will mislead any reader who does not know it is Pydantic. Use 'Field(default_factory=list)' to make the intent unambiguous to a reader who is just looking at the code.

issues.description: No test exercises the GKE MANUAL branch or the zero-interface branch; the truth table is not closed.
issues.detail: Tests cover 1-NIC PASS, 2-NIC FAIL, 3-NIC FAIL, mixed. The MANUAL path for gke- prefix and the empty-interfaces path are unexercised, so the most interesting branches (the ones whose semantics are under dispute above) have no evidence of correctness. Proofs catch what tests miss, but here neither is present for those branches.

review.summary: The check is asymptotically fine (O(n) over instances, O(k) over NICs per instance) and the data-structure addition to Instance is reasonable, but the work is UNDER-AUDITED on three fronts: the name/CheckID disagrees with what the algorithm actually computes; the GKE-vs-non-GKE invariant is detected by name prefix rather than by the authoritative label/metadata; and neither the MANUAL nor the zero-NIC branch is tested. None of these block correctness on the common case, but a careful reader cannot state the invariant from the code as written. Tighten the naming, switch GKE detection to labels, state the loop invariant in a comment, and close the test truth table.
